institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Like hiking a lot and in Tromsø there is an excellant scene for hiking with DNT and amazing scenery. Furthermore, the hospital is a small university hospital with every speciality included which makes a great learning scene.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was good, just a bit tough schedule spending 37 hours at a hospital for 12 weeks, having little excess time and energy for sosialising.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I would say so, I got most from UiT. Regarding the information about the pracital matters at the hopsital, UNN, I had to figure out a lot myself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. Did not attend 'debut wee' due to time constraints, so I am just myself to blame.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden has student housing, different locations and quality, cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived at a dorm where it was not very social, so yeah that depends a lot from the bigger dorms i guess.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The rental market in Tromsø is tough, so I find myself very fortunate to have found cheap student housing, that it was not very social, is only a minor thing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A little confusing using the norwegian platform, but ounce you get an email explaining everything it was good. Also there were some Teams- calls explaining things, which helped.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to do an application through søknadsweb.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email, teams-meetings. Email help to UCPH and UiT (Elin Holm, exchange-coordinator)  was helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100%, got a clinical course designed to meet the demands from UCPH.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For future students, just be careful to show UiT the exact demands from the Logbook, so that UiT knows what to do.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Clinical rotations: departments did not have any schedule for us and we had to figure out one self what to do. Orthopedic ward was especially very bad at this. Hematology was a good place, very little cozy department, where everything was easy to figure out.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations, 12 weeks, 5 weeks internal medicine, 5 weeks surgery, 2 weeks anesthesiology

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less structured, more old-school, you had to be more independent.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of great things through TSI, i did Fjellgruppa, which was great

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: -II-

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fjellgruppa

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Senja, Lyngen. DNT-huts around tromsø, TURBO/BUA to borrow gear, Arctic museum, Universitetsbiblioteket, Main library.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Language was difficult at start, but it got better quite fast.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: TSI/Kraft, I did not sozialise a lot actually.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hierarchy and the hospital departments.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fjellturer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Samskipnaden, housing, I lived at Ørndalen which is a bit sleepy. I think Dramsvegen is a better alternative, seems more social. But anyhow student housing is the thing as the private market is a chaos with air b&b pricing availablity down and prices sky-high.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Public transport with 'Svipper' is actually quite nice, so it might now be needed to bring a car as I did. It is howevery very nice to drive through norway.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Doing weekend trips out in the nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying high with motiviation, when there was nobody looking out for you in the clinic. showing up each day and find initative to join the clinical work.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
